population: all 7,249 retained divergent rows from the C32 sweep

invariant.rule: a false-divergence repair may only REMOVE divergences, never add them
invariant.measured_against: the C32 sweep's own attribution, not the archive's
invariant.the_one_increase: RESOLVED and it was not a violation. Compared per-row against the correct pre-fix baseline (72e56cb2~1, verified to lack obs_rolled_branch), ZERO rows regressed from matched to divergent. The I4_attribution_tie +1 is one row moving LS_capped_lethal_shape -> I4_attribution_tie: a re-attribution between two documented families, both already divergent. The earlier apparent violation came from comparing the sweep's readout attribution against a local re-read -- two different measurement paths -- rather than the same path before and after.
invariant.my_first_reading_was_wrong: I initially reported I1 and LS_capped_lethal_shape as RISING. That compared against the ARCHIVE's counts instead of the sweep's. Against the sweep both fall sharply -- I1 333 -> 96, LS_capped_lethal_shape 501 -> 461 -- which shows the leak was inflating four families at once, not only the structural one.

does_not_reach_a_pass: 515 unattributed rows remain against a required zero, and the C32 run independently failed on coverage 0.9587 against a 0.97 floor, on seven family bounds calibrated from the archive, and on eighteen malformed predicted_class entries. This fix touches none of those.

incidental_finding.context: Surfaced while re-reading retained states. Caught and counted rather than crashing the run, but it is a real panic on real states, and it is the shape open PR #1008 (contain poke-engine panics in the native search) addresses. Recorded here because it was found incidentally and would otherwise be lost.

c34_clear_to_ship: Yes on the invariant. Still needs a registration cycle -- freeze, contract, calibration, attestation -- before any sweep, and does not by itself reach a PASS.
